description: Happy baby stretch for pelvic floor relaxation: how to do it, how it should feel, common mistakes, and easier and harder versions for tight hips.
intro: Happy baby is a lying-down stretch where you hold your feet and let your knees open toward your armpits. It opens the inner thighs and hips and lets the pelvic floor lengthen. It does not build strength; it helps tight muscles let go.
feel: You should feel a gentle stretch in your inner thighs and hips, with your lower back and head resting on the floor. You should not feel neck strain, groin pain or breath holding. Self-check: on each inhale, notice a light widening at the base of your pelvis; on the exhale, let it soften rather than tighten.

mistakes.right: Hold lightly and let the weight of your legs open the hips.

mistakes.wrong: Lifting your head off the floor
mistakes.right: Keep your head down. If you cannot reach your feet, hold your ankles, shins or the backs of your thighs.
Rock slowly and only a little, or stay still.

easier: Hold the backs of your thighs, or do one leg at a time with the other foot on the floor. A small pillow under your head helps a tense neck.
harder: Hold the full minute with slower, longer exhales. You can also gently straighten one leg at a time while the pelvic floor stays relaxed.
who: Good for runners and cyclists with tight hips, people who sit a lot, and anyone whose pelvic floor feels tense or hard to relax.
skip: Skip or modify it if you have hip or groin pain, a hernia or recent abdominal or pelvic surgery. In later pregnancy ask your midwife or doctor first; after birth, wait until you are cleared. Stop if it hurts.

faq.q: Is happy baby good for the pelvic floor?
faq.a: It can help the pelvic floor relax and lengthen, which is useful if it is tight. It does not build strength.
Yes. Men carry pelvic floor tension too, often from sitting, stress or heavy lifting. It is a simple way to give those muscles a break after a workout.
